items.title: Dave Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, Wilton, Connecticut, November 21, 2001

ctx.x: Boy that’s exciting. © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Yeah. Yesterday we found out we’re not doing my Easter cantata in Vienna, which was very disappointing to Russell Gloyd, our conductor, but he said, “well then we’ll record it with the London Symphony Orchestra.” I’m trying to make up my mind whether to do the Easter cantata, which is called “Beloved Son” or “Tongues of Fire,” which is about after Christ comes back and fire descends on the disciples and they all speak in tongues and everything. That’s a very different kind of cantata. And I think it’s only been…

A recent quote that you had about a CD of yours called “The Crossing,” you said it’s so important to have this message of freedom going all over the world, prophetic I think, even more important these days I think.
